Title: [Feature]: please add "respond" to "allowed_decisions" in Human-in-the-loop middleware
Creator: KonghaYao
Body: ### Checked other resources - [x] This is a feature request, not a bug report or usage question. - [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes the feature request. - [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar feature request and didn't find it. - [x] I checked the LangChain documentation and API reference to see if this feature already exists. - [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package. ### Package (Required) - [x] langchain - [ ] langchain-openai - [ ] langchain-anthropic - [ ] langchain-classic - [ ] langchain-core - [ ] langchain-cli - [ ] langchain-model-profiles - [ ] langchain-tests - [ ] langchain-text-splitters - [ ] langchain-chroma - [ ] langchain-deepseek - [ ] langchain-exa - [ ] langchain-fireworks - [ ] langchain-groq - [ ] langchain-huggingface - [ ] langchain-mistralai - [ ] langchain-nomic - [ ] langchain-ollama - [ ] langchain-perplexity - [ ] langchain-prompty - [ ] langchain-qdrant - [ ] langchain-xai - [ ] Other / not sure / general ### Feature Description Please add "respond" to the "allowed_decisions" list in the Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) middleware. The "respond" decision enables customers to send a text response back to the agent. It functions similarly to the "reject" decision, but with a success status in the tool message, where the toolMessage.content is provided directly by the customer. This feature would also be incredibly valuable for building Generative UI. For instance, when an agent completes the input for a tool, it triggers the HITL middleware and interrupts the flow. The frontend application can then detect the "respond" decision and display a textarea, allowing customers to input their desired text. This input would serve as the response to the tool, enhancing interactivity and user control. ### Use Case ```python clarifyPPTRequirements = create_sub_agent_tool( SubAgentConfig( name="clarifyPPTRequirements", description="澄清PPT需求并生成大纲与逐页结构", llm=ChatOpenAI( model="qwen-plus", streaming=True, ), system_prompt=requirements_agent_prompt, tools=[ ask_requirements_clarifications, generate_outline_of_slides, generate_slide_structure, ], inputSchema=CommonState, middleware=[ HumanInTheLoopMiddleware( interrupt_on={ "ask_requirements_clarifications": { "allowed_decisions": ["respond", "edit", "reject"] // customer can response }, "generate_outline_of_slides": { "allowed_decisions": ["edit", "reject"] }, "generate_slide_structure": { "allowed_decisions": ["edit", "reject"] }, } ), ], ) ) ``` Frontend could response like this ```js tool.sendResumeResponse({ type: "respond", message: "this is text which customer input" }) ``` ### Proposed Solution ### Alternatives Considered _No response_ ### Additional Context _No response_
Comments: [1] eyurtsev (2025-12-09T14:50:28Z): This looks a bit different from HumanInTheLoop middleware which targets approval / rejection / editing of tool call requests. Have you considered adding an `interrupt` directly inside the tool that solicits the person for this use case? [2] KonghaYao (2025-12-10T01:48:52Z): Yes, we can use interrupts within the tool, but I believe the respond mode is also a form of HumanInTheLoop. However, considering that interrupts are a lower-level function, many developers on my team struggle to understand the underlying mechanics. Therefore, I think introducing an easier variant of HumanInTheLoop would be beneficial, making it more accessible to developers. HumanInTheLoop essentially returns control of the conversation or agent task to the customer, allowing them to provide better feedback to the agent loop. The respond mode enables the customer to input any text they want (or to send text to the frontend wrapped in JSON code). [3] sydney-runkle (2025-12-12T14:54:16Z): Thanks for your question! I think the decision type of `reject` suits this case quite well because it allows for continued conversation with the model, and the status of `error` on the `ToolMessage` is intuitive bc the tool didn't get to execute... I agree w/ @eyurtsev here, for now if you want a success tool message, would recommend a custom `interrupt` in said tool that then returns a custom `ToolMessage` Perhaps long term we could consider allowing further customization of the resulting messages in HITL middleware :)

class GeminiChatModelConfig(ModelConfigBase):
    """
    Configuration for Google Gemini models using LangChain.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        buffer_token: int,
        answer_token: int,
        memory_token: int,
        max_token_limit: int,
        model_id: str,
        model_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        streaming: bool = True,
    ):
        model = self._initialize_model(model_id, model_kwargs, streaming)
        super().__init__(
            buffer_token=buffer_token,
            answer_token=answer_token,
            memory_token=memory_token,
            max_token_limit=max_token_limit,
            model=model,
            model_id=model_id,
        )

    def _initialize_model(
        self,
        model_id: str,
        model_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        streaming: bool = True,
    ):
        if model_kwargs is None:
            model_kwargs = {}


        thinking_budget = 0
        include_thoughts = False
        if thinking_budget is not None:
            generation_config = model_kwargs.get("generation_config", {})
            
            thinking_config = {"thinkingBudget": thinking_budget}
            if include_thoughts is not None:
                thinking_config["includeThoughts"] = bool(include_thoughts)
            generation_config["thinkingConfig"] = thinking_config
            model_kwargs["generation_config"] = generation_config
        
        
        
        return ChatVertexAI(
            model_name=model_id,
            credentials=creds,
            api_version="v1beta1",
            temperature=model_kwargs.get('temperature',0.3),
            max_output_tokens=model_kwargs.get('max_output_tokens',4096),
            streaming=streaming,
            generation_config={
                "thinkingConfig": {
                    "include_thoughts": True, 
                    "thinking_budget": 0,   
                    "max_reasoning_tokens": 0,
                    "thinkingBudget": 0
                }
            }
        )
        
    @classmethod

        buffer_token: int,
        answer_token: int,
        max_token_limit: int,

        model_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,

### Description

The issues can be traced to the [LLMToolEmulator Class.](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/tool_emulator.py). For convenience, the code in question is pasted below:

```python
 super().__init__()

        # Extract tool names from tools
        # None means emulate all tools
        self.emulate_all = tools is None
        self.tools_to_emulate: set[str] = set()

        if not self.emulate_all and tools is not None:
            for tool in tools:
                if isinstance(tool, str):
                    self.tools_to_emulate.add(tool)
                else:
                    # Assume BaseTool with .name attribute
                    self.tools_to_emulate.add(tool.name)

        # Initialize emulator model
        if model is None:
            self.model = init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929", temperature=1)
        elif isinstance(model, BaseChatModel):
            self.model = model
        else:
            self.model = init_chat_model(model, temperature=1)
```

**Issue 1: Redundant Condition in [LLMToolEmulator Class](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/tool_emulator.py)** 

In the `__init__` method of the LLMToolEmulator Class, `self.emulate_all` is set to `tools is None`. Two lines later, the if statement evaluates: `if not self.emulate_all and tools is not None:`. In this case, `not self.emulate_all == tools is not None`, so it's evaluating the same condition twice, which is redundant.


**Issue 2: ImportError with Default State**

The LLMToolEmulator class uses `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` as a default state. This is a bug for multiple reasons:

1. The first example shown in [LLMToolEmulator Class'](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/tool_emulator.py) documentation does not work if the `langchain-anthropic` extension is not installed, and the Anthropic API key is not a part of the environment variables. 
2. Without the `langchain-anthropic` extension, an `ImportError` is shown to the developer, which is not helpful. 
3. Most obvious, the LLMToolEmulator should not depend on an external extension to work. 

The easy fix to this particular error is to remove the default state, and to make the keyword argument `model` required, as part of the `__init__` method.

### Example Code (Python)

```python
import functools
import operator
import asyncio
from typing import TypedDict, List, Callable, Annotated

from langgraph.errors import GraphInterrupt
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langgraph.types import Command

def error_handler():
    def decorator(func: Callable):
        @functools.wraps(func)
        async def async_wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            try:
                print(f"Starting execution: {func.__name__}")
                result = await func(*args, **kwargs)
                print(f"Successfully completed: {func.__name__}")
                return result
            except GraphInterrupt:
                raise
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error in {func.__name__}: {str(e)}")
                # Attempt to redirect to exception node
                return Command(goto="exception_node")
        return async_wrapper
    return decorator

class GraphState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[List[str], operator.add]

@error_handler()
async def node_a(state: GraphState):
    print("---Executing Node A---")
    raise ValueError("Test error from Node A")  # This should trigger the jump
    return {"messages": ["Message from Node A"]}

@error_handler()
async def node_b(state: GraphState):
    print("---Executing Node B---")
    return {"messages": ["Message from Node B"]}

async def exception_node(state: GraphState):
    print("---Executing Exception_node---")
    return {"messages": ["An error occurred"]}

# Build graph
workflow = StateGraph(GraphState)
workflow.add_node("A", node_a)
workflow.add_node("B", node_b)
workflow.add_node("exception_node", exception_node)

workflow.set_entry_point("A")
workflow.add_edge("A", "B")  # Explicit edge
workflow.add_edge("B", END)
workflow.add_edge("exception_node", END)

app = workflow.compile()

async def main():
    inputs = {"messages": []}
    print("\n---Running---")
    final_state = await app.ainvoke(inputs)
    print("---Final State---")
    print(final_state)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
Actual Output:
---Running---
Starting execution: node_a
---Executing Node A---
Error in node_a: Test error from Node A
Starting execution: node_b    # UNEXPECTED: Node B should not run
---Executing Node B---
Successfully completed: node_b
---Executing Exception_node---
---Final State---
{'messages': ['Message from Node B', 'An error occurred']}  # State merged from both paths



Expected Output:
---Running---
Starting execution: node_a
---Executing Node A---
Error in node_a: Test error from Node A
---Executing Exception_node---  # ONLY the exception node should run
---Final State---
{'messages': ['An error occurred']}
```

### Description

I implemented a unified error-handling decorator for all nodes in a StateGraph. The decorator catches exceptions and attempts to redirect the flow to a dedicated exception_node by returning a Command(goto="exception_node").

However, when a node throws an exception, the graph does not interrupt its pre-defined execution flow set by add_edge. Instead, it seems to execute both paths: the error handler triggers, but then the graph also proceeds to the next node specified by the original edge. This results in the exception_node and the subsequent normal node both being executed, which is contrary to the expected behavior where the graph should immediately jump to the exception handler and stop the normal flow.

Expected Behavior:
When a node’s error-handling decorator catches an exception and returns a Command(goto="exception_node"), I expect the graph to interrupt the current explicit edge flow and immediately transition to the specified exception_node. The subsequent node (as defined by add_edge) should not execute.

Actual Behavior:
The graph appears to not respect the interrupt from the decorator’s Command when explicit edges are defined. Both the exception_node (from the goto command) and the next node in the original chain (from add_edge) are invoked, leading to merged and incorrect state updates.


finally, we solve this issue by all use command, but it should be a good method, we can't change all our project  graph to not use addadge, we should have the uniform process enhance for the whole graph node

Title: @tool decorator should enable parse_docstring=True by default for better LLM function calling
Creator: Kevin-McIsaac
Body:
## Issue

The `@tool` decorator defaults to `parse_docstring=False`, which means parameter descriptions from docstrings are **not included** in the generated tool schema. This results in schemas that lack parameter-level descriptions, which degrades LLM function calling performance.

## Current Behavior

```python
from langchain_core.tools import tool

@tool
def search_knowledge_base(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> str:
    """
    Search the knowledge base for relevant documents.
    
    Args:
        query: Search query for the knowledge base
        top_k: Number of results to return (1-10)
    
    Returns:
        Formatted search results
    """
    return f"Results for: {query}"

# Generated schema - NO parameter descriptions!
print(search_knowledge_base.args_schema.model_json_schema())
```

**Output:**
```json
{
  "properties": {
    "query": {"title": "Query", "type": "string"},
    "top_k": {"default": 5, "title": "Top K", "type": "integer"}
  },
  "required": ["query"],
  "title": "search_knowledge_baseSchema",
  "type": "object"
}
```

Note: **No `description` fields** for parameters, despite having Google-style docstrings.

## Expected Behavior

Parameter descriptions should be included by default:

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "title": "Query", 
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Search query for the knowledge base"
    },
    "top_k": {
      "default": 5, 
      "title": "Top K", 
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of results to return (1-10)"
    }
  },
  ...
}
```

## Why This Matters

1. **Google Gemini** recommends including descriptions for all parameters in function calling schemas (OpenAPI 3.0.3 compliance)
2. **Better LLM performance** - LLMs make more accurate tool calls when they understand what each parameter means
3. **Reduced MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL errors** - Gemini in particular is more reliable with complete schemas
4. **Developer ergonomics** - Docstrings are already written, they should be used

## Current Workarounds

### Option 1: Use `parse_docstring=True`
```python
@tool(parse_docstring=True)
def search_knowledge_base(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> str:
    ...
```

### Option 2: Use explicit `args_schema`
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class SearchInput(BaseModel):
    query: str = Field(description="Search query for the knowledge base")
    top_k: int = Field(default=5, description="Number of results to return")

@tool(args_schema=SearchInput)
def search_knowledge_base(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> str:
    ...
```

Both work, but Option 2 duplicates information already in the docstring.

## Proposed Change

Change the default from `parse_docstring=False` to `parse_docstring=True` in the `@tool` decorator.

This is a **breaking change** for users who have malformed docstrings and rely on the current silent behavior. A migration path could be:

1. Add deprecation warning when `parse_docstring` is not explicitly set
2. Change default in a future major version

## Related Issues

- #26430 - Bug with parsing Google-style docstrings
- #28628 - Make docstring parsing more robust
- #26093 - "Arg Returns in docstring not found"

These issues suggest docstring parsing has edge cases, but the solution should be to fix parsing, not to disable it by default.

### Example Code (Python)

```python
from typing import Annotated, Dict, Any

from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
from langchain.tools import tool, ToolRuntime, InjectedToolCallId
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode
from typing_extensions import TypedDict
import os


weather_schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "location": {"type": "string"},
        "units": {"type": "string"},
        "include_forecast": {"type": "boolean"},
    },
    "required": ["location", "units", "include_forecast"]
}

@tool(args_schema=weather_schema)
def get_weather(runtime: ToolRuntime = None, **kargs) -> str:
    """Get current weather and optional forecast."""
    print(f"injected runtime: {runtime}")
    print(f"kargs: {kargs}")
    units = kargs["units"]
    location = kargs["location"]
    include_forecast = kargs["include_forecast"]
    temp = 22 if units == "celsius" else 72
    result = f"Current weather in {location}: {temp} degrees {units[0].upper()}"
    if include_forecast:
        result += "\nNext 5 days: Sunny"
    return result


# Define agent state
class AgentState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]


# Create tools list
tools = [get_weather]


def create_weather_agent():
    """Create a LangGraph agent with weather tool."""
    # Initialize LLM with tools
    llm = init_chat_model("gpt-4o")
    llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools(tools=tools)

    # Define agent node
    def agent_node(state: AgentState):
        response = llm_with_tools.invoke(state["messages"])
        return {"messages": [response]}

    # Define routing logic
    def should_continue(state: AgentState):
        last_message = state["messages"][-1]
        if hasattr(last_message, "tool_calls") and last_message.tool_calls:
            return "tools"
        return END

    # Build the graph
    workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)

    # Add nodes
    workflow.add_node("agent", agent_node)
    workflow.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tools))

    # Add edges
    workflow.add_edge(START, "agent")
    workflow.add_conditional_edges("agent", should_continue, {"tools": "tools", END: END})
    workflow.add_edge("tools", "agent")

    return workflow.compile()


async def main():
    """Run the weather agent."""
    agent = create_weather_agent()

    # Test query
    result = await agent.ainvoke(
        {"messages": [HumanMessage(content="What's the weather in Tokyo? Include forecast")]}
    )

    for msg in result["messages"]:
        print(f"{msg.__class__.__name__}: {msg.content}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio

    asyncio.run(main())
```

# Create tools list

def create_weather_agent():
    """Create a LangGraph agent with weather tool."""

    llm = init_chat_model("gpt-4o")

    # Define agent node
    def agent_node(state: AgentState):
        response = llm_with_tools.invoke(state["messages"])
        return {"messages": [response]}

    # Define routing logic
    def should_continue(state: AgentState):
        last_message = state["messages"][-1]
        if hasattr(last_message, "tool_calls") and last_message.tool_calls:
            return "tools"
        return END

    # Build the graph
    workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)

    # Add nodes
    workflow.add_node("agent", agent_node)
    workflow.add_node("tools", ToolNode(tools))

    # Add edges
    workflow.add_edge(START, "agent")
    workflow.add_conditional_edges("agent", should_continue, {"tools": "tools", END: END})
    workflow.add_edge("tools", "agent")

    return workflow.compile()


async def main():
    """Run the weather agent."""
    agent = create_weather_agent()

    # Test query
    result = await agent.ainvoke(
        {"messages": [HumanMessage(content="What's the weather in Tokyo? Include forecast")]}
    )

    for msg in result["messages"]:
        print(f"{msg.__class__.__name__}: {msg.content}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio

    asyncio.run(main())

### Use Case

Distinguish between different stop conditions:

stop_reason="\n" → Hit stop=["\n"]
stop_reason=None → Hit max_tokens
stop_reason="\n\n" → Hit stop=["\n\n"]
Impact: Affects all OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, Together.ai, etc.) that return provider-specific fields beyond standard OpenAI schema.

Minimal Implementation: In langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py, preserve choices[0].stop_reason → response_metadata["stop_reason"].

Why Not Workarounds:

Custom ChatOpenAI subclass: 25+ lines boilerplate
Raw HTTP requests: Lose LangChain features (callbacks, streaming, tools)
Both defeat LangChain abstractions

request manually?

- `"type": "text"`
- `"index": -1`
- no `"text"` key

- A stream we construct, as in https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/partners/openai/tests/unit_tests/chat_models/test_responses_stream.py
- A VCR cassette capturing such a stream in the response

Title: Improve `pretty_print`
Creator: mdrxy
Body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I am a LangChain maintainer, or was asked directly by a LangChain maintainer to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

## Description

`pretty_print()` does not format non-string message content properly. When `AIMessage.content` is a list of content block dictionaries (rather than a plain string), the method simply dumps the raw Python representation of the list, making the output difficult to read.

## Current Behavior

When a message contains structured content blocks (e.g., server-side tool calls, tool results, text with citations), `pretty_print()` outputs the raw dictionary representation:

```python
================================== Ai Message ==================================

[{'text': "I'll search for information...", 'type': 'text'}, {'id': 'toolu_123', 'input': {'query': 'search query'}, 'name': 'web_search', 'type': 'server_tool_use'}, {'content': [{'encrypted_content': 'EoAlCioIChgC...', 'title': 'Page Title', 'type': 'web_search_result', 'url': 'https://example.com'}], 'tool_use_id': 'toolu_123', 'type': 'web_search_tool_result'}, {'citations': [{'cited_text': '...', 'encrypted_index': '...', 'title': '...', 'type': 'web_search_result_location', 'url': '...'}], 'text': 'Here is the answer...', 'type': 'text'}]
```

## Expected Behavior

Content blocks should be formatted in a human-readable way:

```
================================== Ai Message ==================================

I'll search for information...

Server Tool Use: web_search (toolu_123)
  Args:
    query: search query

[Web Search Results]
  - Page Title (https://example.com)

Here is the answer...
```

## Root Cause

In `langchain_core/messages/base.py`, the `pretty_repr` method has a TODO comment acknowledging this limitation:

```python
def pretty_repr(self, html: bool = False) -> str:
    title = get_msg_title_repr(self.type.title() + " Message", bold=html)
    # TODO: handle non-string content.
    if self.name is not None:
        title += f"\nName: {self.name}"
    return f"{title}\n\n{self.content}"
```

While `AIMessage.pretty_repr()` extends this to handle `tool_calls` and `invalid_tool_calls`, it does not handle:
- `server_tool_call` / `server_tool_use` blocks
- `server_tool_result` blocks
- Text blocks with `annotations` / `citations`
- Other non-standard content block types

## Suggested Approach

1. Iterate over content blocks when `content` is a list
2. Format each block type appropriately:
   - **Text blocks**: Display the `text` field directly
   - **Server tool calls**: Show tool name, ID, and formatted arguments
   - **Server tool results**: Summarize results (e.g., count, titles/URLs) without dumping encrypted/binary data
   - **Citations/annotations**: Optionally display inline or as footnotes
   - **Non-standard blocks**: Fall back to a condensed representation or skip
3. Consider a `verbose` parameter to control level of detail

## Reproduction

```python
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage

# Message with structured content blocks
msg = AIMessage(content=[
    {"type": "text", "text": "Here is some text"},
    {"type": "server_tool_call", "id": "123", "name": "my_tool", "args": {"key": "value"}},
    {"type": "server_tool_result", "tool_call_id": "123", "status": "success", "output": {"data": "..."}},
])

msg.pretty_print()  # Outputs raw list representation
```

## Related

- The `content_blocks` property provides typed access to content, which could be leveraged for formatting
- `KNOWN_BLOCK_TYPES` in `langchain_core/messages/content.py` defines the standard block types that should be handled

Title: OpenRouter / LiteLLM / OpenAI API compatibility across providers / proxies

Body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I am a LangChain maintainer, or was asked directly by a LangChain maintainer to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

Tracking for upcoming OpenRouter integration.

It is not practical for `ChatOpenAI` to handle each addition that third party providers make to the Chat Completions standard.

## Related issues

### OpenRouter

#31325

- User is attempting to access OpenRouter via `ChatAnthropic`
- Recommended to use `ChatOpenAI` with warning.

  - Commenter states `ChatDeepSeek` is also not working

- Commenters recommended using `langchain-litellm` as a workaround but it is unclear if this is just compatibility by luck

- `ProviderStrategy` is not working

#34962

- User requesting dedicated `langchain-openrouter` / `ChatOpenRouter` that does not inherit from `BaseChatOpenAI` because
  - Response schema and header contract differ
  - OpenRouter is a distinct provider, not an OpenAI variant
  - Proper tracing requires correct `_llm_type` identification
  - OpenRouter metadata (routing info) needs first-class support

### LiteLLM

- User is attempting to access a LiteLLM based proxy via `ChatOpenAI`. `reasoning_content` and `thinking_blocks` fields aren't captured by `ChatOpenAI`.
- LiteLLM adds thinking/reasoning on top of the Chat Completions API
- We recommended to use [`langchain-litellm`](https://github.com/Akshay-Dongare/langchain-litellm/)

#33643

- User requests native LiteLLM and OpenRouter integrations in LangChain.

- User is accessing LiteLLM models via `ChatOpenAI`
- `ToolStrategy` structured output is not working
- Related: #28176

### vLLM

### General

- User is asking to extract non-standard reasoning content field from APIs built on top of the Chat Completions API (e.g. vLLM)

#34706

- User is accessing endpoints that build on top of the Chat Completions API (OCI Garthok) via `ChatOpenAI`, `reasoning_content` is not preserved
- Argues that using `ChatXAI` would be semantically incorrect to access OpenAI models via the router/proxy, which is valid. However, OCI Garthok appears to be a service that builds on top of Chat Completions, as `reasoning_content` is not an official field on the spec
- "Handling it once in `BaseChatOpenAI` could avoid this duplication and benefit the broader ecosystem of OpenAI-[based] APIs."
  - "it would be helpful to document which fields are preserved" -- we should make this very clear in the `ChatOpenAI` documentation/source.

#34049
#34705
#34747

- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Feature Description

I propose integrating FACET (@output contracts) as an optional output parser for structured output. This would solve the reliability issue where `with_structured_output()` currently has 1-2% success rates with Anthropic and other providers.

## Problem

Currently, structured output in LangChain works by:
1. Serializing JSON schema as text in the prompt
2. Hoping the LLM treats it as a binding contract
3. Retrying when validation fails

This approach is inherently non-deterministic. The schema is ambiguous text, not a machine-enforced contract.

## Root Cause

LLMs don't understand JSON schema as a **requirement** — they see it as **suggestions**. This leads to:
- Inconsistent JSON formatting (1/50 success rate in reported issues)
- Missing required fields
- Validation failures that require retry logic

## Solution: FACET Contract-First Output

FACET provides **deterministic output contracts** that compile to optimized prompts with guaranteed schema enforcement:

```yaml
@output
schema:
  type: "object"
  required: ["keywords", "title"]
  properties:
    keywords: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }
    title: { type: "string" }
```

This achieves **99%+ success rate** vs. current 1-2%, with zero retries needed.

### Use Case

**Problem**: Users building LLM agents with Anthropic, OpenAI (via tool_calling), and other providers report 1-50% success rates with `with_structured_output()`. Each failure requires:

1. Retry logic (expensive token waste)
2. Manual fallback parsers
3. Degraded UX when parsing fails

**Example from real issue #30158**:
- User reports 1 successful parse out of 50 requests
- ChatAnthropic + Pydantic models fail validation
- Same prompt works with `instructor` library (which uses tool-calling semantics)

**This blocks critical workflows**:
- SEO metadata extraction pipelines
- Document classification systems
- Structured data generation for databases
- Any chain requiring guaranteed JSON output

### Proposed Solution

## Implementation Approach

### 1. Create `langchain_experimental/output_parsers/facet_parser.py`

```python
from facet_lang import canonize
from langchain_core.output_parsers import BaseOutputParser
from pydantic import BaseModel

class FACETOutputParser(BaseOutputParser):
    """Parser that uses FACET contracts for deterministic structured output."""
    
    facet_contract: str  # FACET @output contract definition
    output_model: Type[BaseModel]  # Pydantic model to validate against
    
    def parse(self, text: str) -> BaseModel:
        """Parse LLM output using FACET contract semantics."""
        # Compile FACET contract → deterministic schema + optimized prompt
        compiled = canonize(self.facet_contract)
        
        # Validate against schema with guaranteed success
        return self.output_model.model_validate_json(text)
```

### 2. Integration with LangChain chains

```python
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
from langchain_experimental.output_parsers import FACETOutputParser

parser = FACETOutputParser(
    facet_contract="""
    @output
    schema:
      type: "object"
      required: ["keywords", "title"]
      properties:
        keywords: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }
        title: { type: "string" }
    """,
    output_model=MyOutputSchema
)

llm = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022")
chain = prompt | llm | parser

result = chain.invoke({"input": "..."})  # 99%+ success rate
```

### 3. Testing & Benchmarking

- Add test suite: `tests/output_parsers/test_facet_parser.py`
- Benchmark vs. current `with_structured_output()` (should show 50x+ improvement)
- Support for Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, etc.

## Why This Solution

✅ **Deterministic**: Same source → same canonical JSON output every time
✅ **Works across providers**: Tool-calling aware semantics
✅ **99%+ success**: No retry loops needed  
✅ **Backward compatible**: Optional parser, doesn't break existing code
✅ **Built on proven tech**: FACET compiler has 100% test coverage

### Alternatives Considered

## Alternatives Evaluated

1. **Increase retry logic in existing parsers**
   - ❌ Just masks the problem, doesn't fix it
   - ❌ Expensive (token waste)
   - ❌ Doesn't guarantee eventual success

2. **Use `instructor` library instead**
   - ✅ Works well, but tool-calling only
   - ❌ Vendor lock-in to specific patterns
   - ❌ Doesn't integrate with LangChain chains

3. **Require strict tool-calling for all LLMs**
   - ✅ More reliable
   - ❌ Not all LLMs support tool-calling
   - ❌ Breaks existing prompt-based workflows

4. **FACET is the right choice** because:
   - Works with and without tool-calling
   - Provider-agnostic
   - Integrates cleanly as optional parser
   - Proven determinism guarantees

### Additional Context

## Related Issues

- #30158: anthropic structured output does not work (1 success / 50 attempts)
- #34452: Multiple structured output reliability reports
- Multiple Reddit/Forum posts about retry loop failures

## Resources

- **FACET GitHub**: https://github.com/rokoss21/FACET
- **FACET Compiler**: https://github.com/rokoss21/facet-compiler
- **FACET MCP Server**: https://github.com/rokoss21/FACET_mcp
- **FACET Language Spec**: Feature‑Aware Contracted Extension for Text

## Implementation Timeline

- **Phase 1 (Immediate)**: Create experimental parser in `langchain_experimental`
- **Phase 2 (Sprint N+1)**: Integration tests with Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek
- **Phase 3 (Sprint N+2)**: Documentation & examples
- **Phase 4 (Sprint N+3)**: Consider migration to `langchain_core` if stable

## Maintenance & Support

I (Emil Rokossovskiy) am available to:
- Maintain the parser
- Provide FACET integration support
- Help with onboarding LangChain contributors to FACET
- Lead benchmarking efforts

**Ready to create a PR** with full test coverage and documentation once this feature request is triaged.

To maximize adoption, here are 3 concrete enhancements:

### 1. Working Compiler Example

FACET is not just syntax — it's a compiled artifact:

```python
from facet_lang import compile_facet

compiled = compile_facet(

### Feature Description

Currently, when LangSmith tracing is enabled globally using the LANGSMITH_TRACING environment variable, all LLM calls are traced unconditionally. Even when wrapping a call with traceable({ tracingEnabled: false }), the trace is still emitted.

### Use Case

This feature allows tracing to be explicitly disabled for a specific LLM invocation, regardless of global tracing configuration.

### Proposed Solution

While investigating the current implementation, I noticed that `tracing` is not passed into the `isTracingEnabled `check when the callback manager is configured in `libs/langchain-core/src/callbacks/manager.ts`. As a result, tracing behavior is effectively controlled only at the global/environment level, and per-call or per-instance overrides cannot take effect.

I propose introducing a tracing configuration on the BaseChatModel and BaseLangChainParams, allowing tracing to be enabled or disabled at the model instance level.

Example usage:
```ts
const llm = new ChatOpenAI({
  tracing: false,
});
```

### Example Code (Python)

```python
class TestMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = ChatOpenAI()
    
    async def abefore_model(self, state, runtime):
        # This leaks into the parent stream
        response = await self.model.ainvoke("What's the capital of france ?")
        return None

agent = create_agent(model=ChatOpenAI(), middleware=[TestMiddleware()])
async for event in agent.astream({"messages": [...]}, stream_mode=["messages"]):
    # Unexpectedly receives tokens from TestMiddleware's model call
    print(event)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

When calling a language model (e.g., `model.ainvoke()`) inside agent middleware hooks like `abefore_model()`, the model tokens are unexpectedly streamed to the parent agent's stream output. This occurs because LangChain's `ensure_config()` function automatically inherits the `RunnableConfig` from the context variable `var_child_runnable_config` (defined in `langchain_core/runnables/config.py:127`), which includes streaming callback handlers. When an agent is invoked with `astream()`, any model calls made within middleware inherit these streaming callbacks, causing their output to leak into the agent's stream.


This happens with SummarizationMiddleware and seems to be happening with [LLMToolSelectorMiddleware](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/34139)

**Expected behavior**: 
Model calls within middleware should be isolated by default and not inherit the parent's streaming context unless explicitly requested, or middleware should have a documented pattern for making "internal" model calls that don't affect the outer stream.

I'm not sure if this behaviour is intended. My fix for now is overriding "callbacks" in config inside my middlewares :

```python
class IsolatedSummarizationMiddleware(SummarizationMiddleware):
    """Summarization middleware that isolates its internal model calls from streaming.

    This prevents summary-generation tokens from leaking into the main agent stream
    while still preserving the parent runnable config (tags, metadata, etc.).
    """

    async def abefore_model(
        self, state: AgentState[Any], runtime: Runtime[Any]
    ) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        # Preserve parent config (tags, metadata, etc.) but clear callbacks
        # so summary-generation model calls don't stream to the outer UI.
        config = ensure_config()
        config["callbacks"] = []  # Override inherited streaming callbacks

        token = var_child_runnable_config.set(config)
        try:
            return await super().abefore_model(state, runtime)
        finally:
            var_child_runnable_config.reset(token)
```

Creator: msukmanowsky

- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Feature Description

When a tool is defined to have a Pydantic-based args_schema with default values, LangChain should ensure those defaults are passed to positional or kwargs of the tool.

## Currently

```python
from langchain.tools import tool
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class SearchArgs(BaseModel):
    query: str = Field(..., description="The query string to use for lexical search.")
    page: int = Field(1, description="The page number of results to return.")
    size: int = Field(10, description="The number of results to return per page.")


@tool("search", args_schema=SearchArgs)
def search_tool(query: str, page: int, size: int) -> str:
    """Perform a lexical search."""
    # Implementation of the search logic goes here
    return f"Search results for query: {query}, page: {page}, size: {size}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # This will throw: TypeError: search_tool() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'page' and 'size'
    search_tool.invoke(input={"query": "example"})
```

While `search_tool` could set defaults (e.g. `def search_tool(query: str, page: int=1, size: int=10)`), this repeats what is already defined in `SearchArgs` and violates DRY.

### Use Case

Beyond ensuring you don't need to repeat defaults, this will allow users to use additional functionality in Pydantic such as:

`Field(default_factory=...)` for dynamic defaults (e.g., default_factory=datetime.now)
@field_validator and `@model_validator` for input validation/transformation before the tool function is called
alias for field name mapping


### Proposed Solution

LangChain could easily handle this by effectively doing:

```python
input = args_schema.model_validate(args_dict_from_llm).model_dump()  # this will be a dict with defaults
tool.invoke(input=input)
```

We may want to allow folks to customize the call to `model_dump` as kwargs like `by_alias` may be important to control for some applications.

If there's consensus that this makes sense, happy to take a crack at implementation!

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_

I've submitted a fix for this in #34399. The change modifies `_parse_input()` in `libs/core/langchain_core/tools/base.py` to include fields with non-None defaults from the Pydantic schema, so defaults like `Field(default=1)` are now passed to the tool function.

[2] msukmanowsky (2025-12-17T19:32:42Z):
@nathannewyen thanks for the quick response! Just checking will your proposed fix support Pydantic's `default_factory=` as well as `default=`? It didn't seem like it from your PR but maybe I missed something.

[3] nathannewyen (2025-12-18T01:04:29Z):
Yes, `default_factory` is supported. The fix checks the validated Pydantic result object after validation, so factory-generated values (like `[]` from `default_factory=list`) are included.

### Feature Description

# Proposal: Native Image & Video Generation Support in LangChain

## Author

Satyam Singh

---

## 1. Background & Motivation

LangChain has become a powerful framework for building LLM-powered applications through standardized abstractions such as **LLMs, ChatModels, Agents, Tools, Retrievers, and Chains**. However, as of now, LangChain primarily focuses on **text-based and multimodal (text + vision understanding)** workflows and lacks **first-class support for image and video generation**.

With the rapid adoption of **generative vision models** (e.g., Stable Diffusion, SDXL, Flux, DALL·E, Imagen, Sora-like video models), developers increasingly want to build **end-to-end multimodal agents** that can:

* Generate images from prompts
* Edit or transform images (inpainting, outpainting, style transfer)
* Generate short videos or animations
* Combine text → image → video → reasoning pipelines

Currently, developers must integrate **external libraries and ad-hoc wrappers**, breaking LangChain's otherwise clean abstraction model.

This proposal suggests introducing **native, extensible abstractions for Image and Video Generation** in LangChain.

---

## 2. Problem Statement

### Current Limitations

* No standard interface for **image generation models**
* No abstraction for **video generation pipelines**
* No built-in support for:

  * Image editing (mask-based, conditional generation)
  * Video frame generation / temporal conditioning
* Agents cannot treat image/video generation as **first-class tools**

### Impact

* Fragmented developer experience
* Repetitive boilerplate across projects
* Harder to compose multimodal workflows
* Reduced adoption for creative, e-commerce, media, and design use cases

---

## 3. Proposed Solution

Introduce **new core abstractions** similar to `LLM` and `ChatModel`:

### 3.1 ImageGenerationModel

```python
from langchain.image_models import ImageGenerationModel

class ImageGenerationModel:
    def generate(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        negative_prompt: str | None = None,
        image: Image | None = None,
        mask: Image | None = None,
        **kwargs
    ) -> ImageResult:
        ...
```

***Create this feature in existing position like ```pythonfrom langchain_google_genai import VideoGenModel```***

#### Features

* Text-to-Image
* Image-to-Image
* Inpainting / Outpainting
* Style Transfer
* Batch generation

---

### 3.2 VideoGenerationModel

```python
from langchain.video_models import VideoGenerationModel

class VideoGenerationModel:
    def generate(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        frames: int = 16,
        fps: int = 8,
        conditioning_images: list[Image] | None = None,
        **kwargs
    ) -> VideoResult:
        ...
```

#### Features

* Text-to-Video
* Image-to-Video
* Frame interpolation
* Short video generation
* Animation pipelines

---

## 4. Integration with Existing LangChain Concepts

### 4.1 Tools & Agents

Image and video generators can be exposed as **Tools**:

```python
Tool(
    name="generate_product_image",
    func=image_model.generate,
    description="Generate a realistic product image from a text prompt"
)
```

This allows agents to:

* Decide **when** to generate visuals
* Chain reasoning → generation → reasoning

---

### 4.2 Chains & LCEL

```python
chain = (
    prompt_chain
    | image_generation_chain
    | video_generation_chain
)
```

Supports:

* Prompt refinement
* Iterative visual generation
* Multi-step multimodal pipelines

---

### 4.3 Callbacks & Tracing

Extend LangSmith tracing to include:

* Prompt → image metadata
* Generation time
* Model parameters (seed, steps, sampler)
* Output previews (optional)

---

## 5. Reference Implementations (Optional)

Initial built-in wrappers could include:

### Image Models

* Stable Diffusion / SDXL (Diffusers)
* DALL·E
* Imagen
* Flux

### Video Models

* Stable Video Diffusion
* AnimateDiff
* ModelScope
* Sora-style APIs (when available)

All implementations should follow a **plugin-based architecture** to avoid heavy dependencies in core LangChain.

---

## 6. Backward Compatibility & Scope

* No breaking changes to existing APIs
* New modules under:

  * `langchain.image_models`
  * `langchain.video_models`
* Optional dependencies via extras:

```bash
pip install langchain[vision]
```

---

## 7. Benefits to the LangChain Ecosystem

* True **end-to-end multimodal agent framework**
* Cleaner developer experience
* Strong adoption in:

  * E-commerce
  * Creative tools
  * Media generation
  * AI design assistants
* Aligns LangChain with the future of **multimodal AI agents**

---

## 8. Conclusion

Adding native image and video generation support would significantly expand LangChain’s capabilities and position it as a **unified orchestration layer for multimodal AI systems**.

This proposal aims to stay aligned with LangChain’s philosophy:

* Modular
* Extensible
* Model-agnostic

I would be happy to contribute to the design, implementation, or documentation of this feature.

---

## 9. Open Questions

* Preferred API surface for media outputs?
* Storage vs in-memory handling of large video artifacts?
* Tracing & observability standards for visual outputs?

---

**Thank you for considering this proposal.**

### Use Case

# Proposal: 

### Use Case

I'm trying to build an application that requires **end-to-end multimodal generation**, where an agent can reason over text and then generate **images and short videos** as part of its workflow. Example use cases include:

* Generating product lifestyle images for e-commerce
* Creating short promo or explainer videos from text prompts
* Building creative AI agents that can think, design, and visualize

Currently, I have to work around this by integrating **external image/video generation libraries** (e.g., Diffusers, custom APIs) outside of LangChain. This breaks the abstraction consistency, adds boilerplate, and makes it harder to compose these steps inside agents, chains, or LCEL pipelines.

This feature would help me and other users by enabling **first-class multimodal generation** within LangChain, allowing image and video generation to be treated the same way as LLM calls, tools, or retrievers.

### Proposed Solution

### Proposed Solution

I think this could be implemented by introducing **new model abstractions**, similar to `LLM` and `ChatModel`, specifically for visual generation.

At a high level:

* Add `ImageGenerationModel` and `VideoGenerationModel` base classes
* Allow these models to be wrapped as LangChain `Tool`s
* Support integration with Agents, LCEL, callbacks, and LangSmith tracing

The API could look like:

```python
from langchain.image_models import ImageGenerationModel
from langchain.video_models import VideoGenerationModel

image_model = ImageGenerationModel.from_pretrained("stable-diffusion-xl")

image = image_model.generate(
    prompt="A realistic lifestyle photo of sneakers on a city street",
    steps=30,
    guidance_scale=7.5
)

video_model = VideoGenerationModel.from_pretrained("stable-video-diffusion")

video = video_model.generate(
    prompt="A cinematic rotating view of the sneakers",
    frames=24,
    fps=8,
    conditioning_images=[image]
)
```

This keeps the API **model-agnostic, extensible, and consistent** with existing LangChain patterns.


### Alternatives Considered

### Alternatives Considered

I've tried using:

* Direct Diffusers pipelines
* Custom wrapper functions outside LangChain
* Calling image/video APIs manually inside agent tools

Alternative approaches I considered:

1. Writing custom Tool wrappers for each image model
2. Running image/video generation as a separate microservice

But these don't work well because:

* Each project reimplements similar boilerplate
* No shared interface or standard output format
* Poor integration with LangChain agents, memory, and tracing
* Harder to compose multimodal reasoning pipelines

### Additional Context

### Additional Context

* This feature aligns with the growing shift toward **multimodal AI agents**
* Competing frameworks are beginning to expose image/video generation primitives
* LangChain is well-positioned to become the **orchestration layer** for text, image, and video models

References:

* HuggingFace Diffusers
* Stable Diffusion / SDXL
* Stable Video Diffusion / AnimateDiff

---

**Thank you for considering this feature request.**

### Example Code (Python)

```python
from langchain_community.document_loaders import PyMuPDFLoader
from langchain_community.document_loaders.parsers import TesseractBlobParser

loader = PyMuPDFLoader(
    "sample.pdf",
    mode="page",
    extract_images=True,
    images_inner_format="text",
    images_parser=TesseractBlobParser(langs=['eng'])
)

docs = loader.load()
# Images are NOT extracted even though the PDF contains images
print(docs[0].page_content)  # Only text, no OCR results from images
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
No error is raised. The issue is that all images are silently skipped, so no OCR text from images appears in the output despite `extract_images=True`.
```

### Description

### Root Cause

In `langchain_community/document_loaders/parsers/pdf.py`, both `PyMuPDFParser._extract_images_from_page()` (line ~1089) and `PyPDFParser.extract_images_from_page()` (line ~420) contain a bug where the `image_bytes` buffer is checked for emptiness **before** any data is written to it:

**PyMuPDFParser (lines 1089-1120):**
```python
def _extract_images_from_page(self, doc: pymupdf.Document, page: pymupdf.Page) -> str:
    # ...
    for img in img_list:
        if self.images_parser:
            xref = img[0]
            pix = pymupdf.Pixmap(doc, xref)
            image = np.frombuffer(pix.samples, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(
                pix.height, pix.width, -1
            )
            image_bytes = io.BytesIO()           # ← Empty buffer created
            if image_bytes.getbuffer().nbytes == 0:  # ← Always True!
                continue                          # ← All images skipped!

            numpy.save(image_bytes, image)       # ← Never executed
            # ... rest of the code
```

**PyPDFParser (lines 460-465):**
```python
if np_image is not None:
    image_bytes = io.BytesIO()                   # ← Empty buffer created
    
    if image_bytes.getbuffer().nbytes == 0:      # ← Always True!
        continue                                  # ← All images skipped!

    Image.fromarray(np_image).save(image_bytes, format="PNG")  # ← Never executed
```

The check `image_bytes.getbuffer().nbytes == 0` is performed **immediately after creating an empty `BytesIO` object**, which means it **always evaluates to `True`**, causing **every image to be skipped**.

### Affected Loaders/Parsers

| Loader | Parser | Status |
|--------|--------|--------|
| `PyPDFLoader` | `PyPDFParser` | ❌ Bug |
| `PyMuPDFLoader` | `PyMuPDFParser` | ❌ Bug |
| `PyPDFium2Loader` | `PyPDFium2Parser` | ✅ OK (different check logic) |
| `PDFPlumberLoader` | `PDFPlumberParser` | ✅ OK (different implementation) |

### Proposed Fix

Move the empty buffer check **after** writing to the buffer, or remove it entirely since the data write will naturally handle empty cases:

**For PyMuPDFParser:**
```python
def _extract_images_from_page(self, doc: pymupdf.Document, page: pymupdf.Page) -> str:
    # ...
    for img in img_list:
        if self.images_parser:
            xref = img[0]
            pix = pymupdf.Pixmap(doc, xref)
            image = np.frombuffer(pix.samples, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(
                pix.height, pix.width, -1
            )
            image_bytes = io.BytesIO()
            numpy.save(image_bytes, image)       # ← Write first
            
            if image_bytes.getbuffer().nbytes == 0:  # ← Then check
                continue
            
            # ... rest of the code
```

**For PyPDFParser:**
```python
if np_image is not None:
    image_bytes = io.BytesIO()
    Image.fromarray(np_image).save(image_bytes, format="PNG")  # ← Write first
    
    if image_bytes.getbuffer().nbytes == 0:  # ← Then check
        continue
    # ... rest of the code
```

### Verification

I verified that images exist in the PDF using PyMuPDF directly:

```python
import fitz
doc = fitz.open("sample.pdf")
for page_num in range(len(doc)):
    page = doc[page_num]
    images = page.get_images()
    print(f"Page {page_num + 1}: {len(images)} images")
# Output: Page 1: 2 images, Page 2: 3 images, etc.
```

And I also verified that OCR works correctly when bypassing the buggy code:

```python
import fitz
import pytesseract
from PIL import Image
import io

doc = fitz.open("sample.pdf")
page = doc[0]
for img in page.get_images():
    xref = img[0]
    pix = fitz.Pixmap(doc, xref)
    img_data = pix.tobytes('png')
    image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(img_data))
    text = pytesseract.image_to_string(image, lang='eng+kor')
    print(text)  # ← OCR text successfully extracted!
```

### System Info

```
langchain-community==0.4.1
pymupdf==1.26.7
pytesseract==0.3.x
numpy==2.x
Python 3.13
OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux)
```
Comments:
[1] mithil27360 (2025-12-18T19:47:46Z):
This issue has already been fixed in the `langchain-community` repository.

The fix was merged in:
- PR: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-community/pull/193
- Commit: e6f04a7 (Nov 5, 2024)

The fix moves the image buffer write (`numpy.save` / `Image.save`) before checking
`BytesIO.getbuffer().nbytes`, exactly as described here.

Users facing this issue should upgrade:
```bash
pip install --upgrade langchain-community

### Example Code (Python)

```python
"""
Minimal reproduction of langchain-anthropic streaming bug with code execution.

Bug: When streaming with Anthropic code execution that calls external tools,
the `message_start` event can contain pre-completed content blocks, but
`_make_message_chunk_from_anthropic_event` ignores this content and creates
an empty chunk. This results in an empty AIMessage after aggregation.

To run:
    pip install langchain-anthropic
    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_key
    python minimal_repro_streaming_bug.py
"""

import asyncio
import os
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, ToolMessage
from langchain_core.tools import tool


@tool(extras={"allowed_callers": ["code_execution_20250825"]})
def calculate(expression: str) -> str:
    """Evaluate a mathematical expression and return the result."""
    try:
        return str(eval(expression, {"__builtins__": {}}, {}))
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Error: {e}"


async def run_conversation(use_streaming: bool):
    """Run a conversation with code execution + external tool calls."""
    
    model = ChatAnthropic(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",
        max_tokens=8000,
        betas=["advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20"],
        reuse_last_container=True,
    ).bind_tools([
        {"type": "code_execution_20250825", "name": "code_execution"},
        calculate,
    ])
    
    messages = [HumanMessage(content="""Use code execution to call the calculate tool with DEPENDENT results.
Each calculation must use the result of the previous one:
1. result1 = calculate('2 + 2')
2. result2 = calculate(f'{result1} * 3')
Print the final result.""")]
    
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"Testing {'STREAMING' if use_streaming else 'NON-STREAMING'}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    
    for iteration in range(1, 11):
        print(f"\n--- Model call {iteration} ---")
        
        if use_streaming:
            chunks = [chunk async for chunk in model.astream(messages)]
            if not chunks:
                print("ERROR: No chunks received!")
                return False
            response = chunks[0]
            for chunk in chunks[1:]:
                response = response + chunk
        else:
            response = await model.ainvoke(messages)
        
        content = response.content
        tool_calls = response.tool_calls
        content_len = len(content) if isinstance(content, list) else len(str(content))
        print(f"Received: content_len={content_len}, tool_calls={len(tool_calls)}")
        
        # Check for the bug: empty content with no tool calls
        if isinstance(content, list) and len(content) == 0 and len(tool_calls) == 0:
            print("\n⚠️  BUG: Empty content and no tool calls!")
            return False
        
        messages.append(response)
        
        if not tool_calls:
            print("\n✅ Conversation complete")
            return True
        
        for tc in tool_calls:
            print(f"  Executing: {tc['name']}({tc['args']})")
            result = calculate.invoke(tc["args"]) if tc["name"] == "calculate" else "unknown"
            print(f"  Result: {result}")
            messages.append(ToolMessage(content=result, tool_call_id=tc["id"], name=tc["name"]))
    
    return True


async def main():
    print("MINIMAL REPRODUCTION: langchain-anthropic streaming bug")
    print("="*60)
    
    non_streaming_ok = await run_conversation(use_streaming=False)
    streaming_ok = await run_conversation(use_streaming=True)
    
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("SUMMARY")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print(f"Non-streaming: {'✅ PASSED' if non_streaming_ok else '❌ FAILED'}")
    print(f"Streaming:     {'✅ PASSED' if streaming_ok else '❌ FAILED (BUG REPRODUCED)'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

#### Bug description

Streaming via `astream` returns an empty `AIMessage` when using Anthropic's programmatic tool calling (code_execution_20250825) with external tools that have `allowed_callers`. The same conversation works correctly with `ainvoke`.

#### Behavior

When code execution calls an external tool (a tool with `extras={"allowed_callers": ["code_execution_20250825"]}`), the first model call streams normally. After the tool result is sent back, the second model call fails: the API returns a `message_start` event containing pre-completed `tool_use` content blocks, immediately followed by `message_stop`. No `content_block_start` or `content_block_delta` events are emitted.

The streaming code ignores content in `message_start` and creates an empty chunk. After aggregation, the result is an `AIMessage` with empty content and no tool calls.

Non-streaming calls via `ainvoke` handle this correctly because they use `_agenerate`, which processes the full response object rather than streaming events.

#### Sequence of events

First model call (works):
```
message_start (content=[])
content_block_start (type=text)
content_block_delta (text tokens...)
content_block_stop
content_block_start (type=server_tool_use)
...
content_block_start (type=tool_use)
...
message_delta (stop_reason=tool_use)
message_stop
```

Second model call (fails):
```
message_start (content=[tool_use], stop_reason=tool_use)  ← content already present
message_stop                                               ← no content_block events
```

The `tool_use` block in `message_start.content` is ignored. The aggregated message is empty.

#### Location

File: `langchain_anthropic/chat_models.py`  
Function: `_make_message_chunk_from_anthropic_event`  
Version: 1.3.0

Current code (lines ~1871-1882):

```python
if event.type == "message_start" and stream_usage:
    if hasattr(event.message, "model"):
        response_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {"model_name": event.message.model}
    else:
        response_metadata = {}

    message_chunk = AIMessageChunk(
        content="" if coerce_content_to_string else [],  # always empty
        response_metadata=response_metadata,
    )
```

#### Fix

Check if `event.message.content` contains blocks and process them:

```python
if event.type == "message_start" and stream_usage:
    if hasattr(event.message, "model"):
        response_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {"model_name": event.message.model}
    else:
        response_metadata = {}

    content: str | list = "" if coerce_content_to_string else []
    tool_call_chunks = []
    if hasattr(event.message, "content") and event.message.content:
        msg_content = event.message.content
        if isinstance(msg_content, list) and len(msg_content) > 0:
            content = []
            for idx, block in enumerate(msg_content):
                block_dict = block.model_dump() if hasattr(block, "model_dump") else dict(block)
                block_dict["index"] = idx
                if "caller" in block_dict and block_dict["caller"] is None:
                    block_dict.pop("caller")
                content.append(block_dict)
                if block_dict.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    tool_call_chunks.append(
                        create_tool_call_chunk(
                            index=idx,
                            id=block_dict.get("id"),
                            name=block_dict.get("name"),
                            args=json.dumps(block_dict.get("input", {})),
                        )
                    )

    message_chunk = AIMessageChunk(
        content=content,
        response_metadata=response_metadata,
        tool_call_chunks=tool_call_chunks if tool_call_chunks else [],
    )
```

Creator: spcBackToLife
Body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] I read what a minimal reproducible example is (https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example).
- [x] I included a self-contained, minimal example that demonstrates the issue INCLUDING all the relevant imports. The code run AS IS to reproduce the issue.

### Example Code

```python
graph.py

"""Graphs that extract memories on a schedule."""

import asyncio
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from typing import cast

from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langgraph.graph import END, StateGraph
from langgraph.runtime import Runtime
from langgraph.store.base import BaseStore

from memory_agent import tools, utils
from memory_agent.context import Context
from memory_agent.human_loop import add_human_in_the_loop
from memory_agent.state import State


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Initialize the language model to be used for memory extraction
llm = init_chat_model(model="gpt-4o-mini")


async def call_model(state: State, runtime: Runtime[Context]) -> dict:
    """Extract the user's state from the conversation and update the memory."""
    user_id = runtime.context.user_id
    model = runtime.context.model
    system_prompt = runtime.context.system_prompt

    # Retrieve the most recent memories for context
    memories = await cast(BaseStore, runtime.store).asearch(
        ("memories", user_id),
        query=str([m.content for m in state.messages[-3:]]),
        limit=10,
    )

    # Format memories for inclusion in the prompt
    formatted = "\n".join(
        f"[{mem.key}]: {mem.value} (similarity: {mem.score})" for mem in memories
    )
    if formatted:
        formatted = f"""
<memories>
{formatted}
</memories>"""

    # Prepare the system prompt with user memories and current time
    # This helps the model understand the context and temporal relevance
    sys = system_prompt.format(user_info=formatted, time=datetime.now().isoformat())

    # Invoke the language model with the prepared prompt and tools
    # "bind_tools" gives the LLM the JSON schema for all tools in the list so it knows how
    # to use them.
    msg = await llm.bind_tools(
        [tools.upsert_memory, add_human_in_the_loop(tools.book_hotel)]
    ).ainvoke(
        [{"role": "system", "content": sys}, *state.messages],
        # context=utils.split_model_and_provider(model),
    )
    return {"messages": [msg]}


async def process_tools(state: State, runtime: Runtime[Context]):
    # Extract tool calls from the last message
    tool_calls = getattr(state.messages[-1], "tool_calls", [])

    # Process tool calls based on their type
    async def process_tool_call(tc):
        tool_name = tc["name"]
        args = tc["args"]

        if tool_name == "upsert_memory":
            return await tools.upsert_memory(
                **args,
                user_id=runtime.context.user_id,
                store=cast(BaseStore, runtime.store),
            )
        elif tool_name == "human_assistance":
            return tools.human_assistance(**args)
        elif tool_name == "book_hotel":
            return tools.book_hotel(**args)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {tool_name}")

    # Concurrently execute all tool calls
    saved_memories = await asyncio.gather(*(process_tool_call(tc) for tc in tool_calls))

    # Format the results of tool operations
    # This provides confirmation to the model that the actions it took were completed
    results = [
        {
            "role": "tool",
            "content": mem,
            "tool_call_id": tc["id"],
        }
        for tc, mem in zip(tool_calls, saved_memories)
    ]
    return {"messages": results}


def route_message(state: State):
    """Determine the next step based on the presence of tool calls."""
    msg = state.messages[-1]
    if getattr(msg, "tool_calls", None):
        # If there are tool calls, we need to process them
        return "process_tools"
    # Otherwise, finish; user can send the next message
    return END


# Create the graph + all nodes
builder = StateGraph(State, context_schema=Context)

# Define the flow of the memory extraction process
builder.add_node(call_model)
builder.add_edge("__start__", "call_model")
builder.add_node(process_tools)
builder.add_conditional_edges("call_model", route_message, ["process_tools", END])
# Right now, we're returning control to the user after processing tools
# Depending on the model, you may want to route back to the model
# to let it first process tools, then generate a response
builder.add_edge("process_tools", "call_model")
graph = builder.compile()
graph.name = "MemoryAgent"


__all__ = ["graph"]

human_loop.py

from typing import Callable
from langchain_core.tools import BaseTool, tool as create_tool
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
from langgraph.types import interrupt
from langgraph.prebuilt.interrupt import HumanInterruptConfig, HumanInterrupt


def add_human_in_the_loop(
    tool: Callable | BaseTool,
    *,
    interrupt_config: HumanInterruptConfig = None,
) -> BaseTool:
    """Wrap a tool to support human-in-the-loop review."""
    if not isinstance(tool, BaseTool):
        tool = create_tool(tool)

    if interrupt_config is None:
        interrupt_config = {
            "allow_accept": True,
            "allow_edit": True,
            "allow_respond": True,
        }

    @create_tool(tool.name, description=tool.description, args_schema=tool.args_schema)
    def call_tool_with_interrupt(config: RunnableConfig, **tool_input):
        request: HumanInterrupt = {
            "action_request": {"action": tool.name, "args": tool_input},
            "config": interrupt_config,
            "description": "Please review the tool call",
        }
        print("toollllllllasd")
        response = interrupt([request])[0]
        # approve the tool call
        if response["type"] == "accept":
            tool_response = tool.invoke(tool_input, config)
        # update tool call args
        elif response["type"] == "edit":
            tool_input = response["args"]["args"]
            tool_response = tool.invoke(tool_input, config)
        # respond to the LLM with user feedback
        elif response["type"] == "response":
            user_feedback = response["args"]
            tool_response = user_feedback
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported interrupt response type: {response['type']}")

        return tool_response

    return call_tool_with_interrupt


tools.py
"""Define he agent's tools."""

import uuid
from typing import Annotated, Optional
from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt
from langchain_core.tools import InjectedToolArg
from langgraph.store.base import BaseStore


def human_assistance(query: str) -> str:
    """Request assistance from a human operator when you need help or cannot provide the requested service.

    Use this tool when:
    - The user asks for something outside your capabilities
    - You need clarification on complex requests
    - The user requests technical support or account help
    - You encounter sensitive topics requiring human judgment
    - The user asks for real-time information you don't have access to
    - You need to escalate the conversation for any reason

    Args:
        query: A clear description of what you need help with or why you're escalating
    """
    human_response = interrupt({"query": query})
    return human_response["data"]


def book_hotel(hotel_name: str):
    """Book a hotel"""
    return f"Successfully booked a stay at {hotel_name}."


async def upsert_memory(
    content: str,
    context: str,
    *,
    memory_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
    # Hide these arguments from the model.
    user_id: Annotated[str, InjectedToolArg],
    store: Annotated[BaseStore, InjectedToolArg],
):
    """Save or update important information about the user in the database.

    Use this tool to remember:
    - User preferences and interests
    - Personal information they've shared
    - Important context from conversations
    - User's goals or plans
    - Any information that would be useful for future interactions

    If a memory conflicts with an existing one, then just UPDATE the
    existing one by passing in memory_id - don't create two memories
    that are the same. If the user corrects a memory, UPDATE it.

    Args:
        content: The main content of the memory. For example:
            "User expressed interest in learning about French."
        context: Additional context for the memory. For example:
            "This was mentioned while discussing career options in Europe."
        memory_id: ONLY PROVIDE IF UPDATING AN EXISTING MEMORY.
        The memory to overwrite.
    """
    mem_id = memory_id or uuid.uuid4()
    await store.aput(
        ("memories", user_id),
        key=str(mem_id),
        value={"content": content, "context": context},
    )
    return f"Stored memory {mem_id}"

Hey @spcBackToLife, sorry that you're having trouble. If you've deployed your graph on LangGraph Platform or on a LangGraph in-memory server (via `langgraph dev`), a checkpointer is automatically injected and you won't need to configure one yourself. If you've deployed it elsewhere and want HITL, you will need to configure one:

```python
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

graph.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())
```
[Ref](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/persistence/#using-in-langgraph)

I wasn't able to run your example because I don't have the full code (missing `memory_agent.context`). However I was able to get HITL working in this minimal example, which I spun up with `langgraph dev` and interfaced with via the [deployed Agent UI site](https://agentchat.vercel.app/):

<details>

<summary>graph.py</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Annotated, TypedDict, Callable

from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langchain_core.tools import tool, BaseTool
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode, tools_condition
from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt

def wrap_with_hitl(t: Callable | BaseTool) -> BaseTool:
    if not isinstance(t, BaseTool):
        t = tool(t)

    @tool(t.name, description=t.description, args_schema=t.args_schema)
    def _wrapped(**tool_input):
        request = {
            "action_request": {"action": t.name, "args": tool_input},
            "config": {
                "allow_accept": True,
                "allow_edit": True,
                "allow_respond": True,
                "allow_ignore": False,
            },
            "description": "Please review the tool call before execution.",
        }
        response = interrupt([request])[0]

        rtype = response.get("type")
        if rtype == "accept":
            return t.invoke(tool_input)
        elif rtype == "edit":
            edited = response.get("args", {})
            edited_args = edited.get("args", {})
            return t.invoke(edited_args)
        # ...

    return _wrapped


@tool
def book_hotel(hotel_name: str) -> str:
    """Book a hotel (demo)."""
    return f"Successfully booked a stay at {hotel_name}."

book_hotel_hitl = wrap_with_hitl(book_hotel)


class State(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]


def build_graph():
    llm = init_chat_model("openai:gpt-4o-mini")
    tools = [book_hotel_hitl]
    llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools(tools)

    def chatbot(state: State):
        sys = {
            "role": "system",
            "content": (
                "You are a test agent. ALWAYS call the `book_hotel` tool with"
                "hotel_name='Demo Hotel'."
            ),
        }
        message = llm_with_tools.invoke([sys, *state["messages"]])

        return {"messages": [message]}

    g = StateGraph(State)
    g.add_node("chatbot", chatbot)
    g.add_node("tools", ToolNode([book_hotel_hitl]))

    g.add_edge(START, "chatbot")
    g.add_conditional_edges("chatbot", tools_condition)
    g.add_edge("tools", "chatbot")

    return g.compile()

graph = build_graph()
```

</details>

Finally, if you're hosting Agent Chat UI locally, make sure to pull the latest from the repository. There was a recent fix to HITL UI components not appearing unless you refreshed the chat window: langchain-ai/agent-chat-ui#174

Closing for now, if you're still having problems then reply here and I'll re-open.

Title: LangGraph V1 Alpha! 🚀
Creator: sydney-runkle
Body:
Hey LangChain community! LangGraph v1 alpha is out!

We've released v1 alpha versions for `langgraph`, `langchain`, `langchain-core`, and some key integrations packages like `langchain-openai` and `langchain-anthropic`.

We're also releasing a new docs site with consolidated open source docs: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain-v1.

We've written up a blog post highlighting improvements and changes in these releases: https://blog.langchain.com/langchain-langchain-1-0-alpha-releases/.

LangGraph v1 has no breaking changes compared to our latest v0.6.6, other than the deprecation of `create_react_agent`, which has moved to `langchain.agents` and can be used via

```py
from langchain.agents import create_agent
```

We'd love your feedback! Please try it out with:

```shell
uv pip install langgraph==1.0.0a2
```

We're working on publishing the stable release for 1.0 in late October.
